newsitem.title: FRANCE: France widens irrigation curbs due to drought fear.
newsitem.headline: France widens irrigation curbs due to drought fear.

text.p: Authorities in the Ile de France region around Paris have started limiting the amount of water farmers can use to irrigate their crops due to early signs of drought, a local government official said on Tuesday.
The action, coupled with similar measures in the grain-rich region of Beauce south of the capital, brings the number of provinces or departments hit by such restrictions to six.
Areas now covered by partial irrigation bans include some of France's most productive arable land.
The list includes Essonne, Yvelines, Seine et Marne, Eure et Loir and Loir et Cher, the official said. In total more than 200 local communities are affected.

Dry weather in recent weeks has encouraged many grain farmers around the capital to tap the water table to refresh rainless crops. Undergound water resources in several farming areas are worryingly low, the official said.
But farmers and market gardeners who grow fruit, vegetables, flowers or medicinal crops are being exempted.
The new rules mean farmers are prevented from sprinkling crops for 48 hours each week between 8 am on Saturdays to 8 am on Mondays, the official said.
From June 17, the irrigation ban will be shortened to 36 hours until the end of the crop season or September 30 at the latest. The official said the curbs would probably start this weekend.
